seo_title: FSSAI Adds Six New Recognised Food Testing Labs
title: FSSAI Amends Its Section 43(1) List, Recognises Six More Food Testing Laboratories
court: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
case_name: Amendment to the List of FSSAI-Recognised Food Testing Laboratories under Section 43(1), FSS Act 2006
citation: Notification dated 05.11.2026, amending S.O. 3648(E) dated 06.12.2016; published in the Gazette of India (Gazette No. 672) dated 06.11.2026
card_summary: FSSAI amended its Section 43(1) list of recognised food testing laboratories, adding six new entries across five states, including Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Kerala. The notification, signed on 5 November 2026, amends the principal list issued under S.O. 3648(E) of 6 December 2016, widening the labs to which Food Safety Officers can send samples for analysis.
card_tip: In a food safety prosecution, check whether the analysing lab was on FSSAI's Section 43(1) list on the date of testing; a report from a lab added or dropped afterward can be challenged on that ground.
verification_notes: The notification date (5 November 2026), the Gazette number (672) and its Gazette date (6 November 2026), and that it amends S.O. 3648(E) of 6 December 2016, are confirmed from the FSSAI-hosted notification PDF itself (a near-primary source). The count of six new laboratory entries and the five states involved (Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Kerala) are reported by Corpseed's secondary summary and are consistent with partial lab entries visible in the primary PDF (a Ghaziabad, UP entry and an Indore, MP entry were independently seen in the document). The specific lab names and registration numbers were not fully legible in either source and are omitted here rather than guessed. A related FSSAI validity order dated 6 November 2026 (recognised-labs list with NABL accreditation status) was noted but not used as a card fact.
